bmt-2016-individual-01.title: Complement
bmt-2016-individual-01.body:
The sum of $1,\dots,29$ is $435$. Numbers coprime to $30$ below $30$ are $1,7,11,13,17,19,23,29$ with sum $120$. So the answer is $435-120=315$.

**Answer: 315**

bmt-2016-individual-02.title: Rewrite the operation
bmt-2016-individual-02.body:
$2ab+a+b=\frac{(2a+1)(2b+1)-1}{2}$. Define $\phi(a)=2a+1$; then $\phi(a\star b)=\phi(a)\phi(b)$, so $\star$ is commutative and associative. Thus $(3\star4)\star5=3\star(4\star5)=(4\star5)\star3=4\star(5\star3)$ and the difference is $0$.

**Answer: 0**

bmt-2016-individual-03.title: Compute the sides
bmt-2016-individual-03.body:
The square has side $1$ and perimeter $4$. The equilateral triangle with area $\frac{\sqrt3}{4}s^2=1$ has $s=\frac{2}{3^{1/4}}$ and perimeter $\frac{6}{3^{1/4}}$. The product is $\frac{24}{3^{1/4}}=8\cdot3^{3/4}=8\sqrt[4]{27}$.

**Answer: $8\sqrt[4]{27}$**

bmt-2016-individual-04.title: Area identity
bmt-2016-individual-04.body:
Let the distances from $P$ to the sides of length $3,4,5$ be $d_3,d_4,d_5$. Splitting the triangle into three pieces: $3d_3+4d_4+5d_5=2\cdot6=12$. Then $d_3+d_4+d_5\ge\frac{3d_3+4d_4+5d_5}{5}=\frac{12}{5}$, with equality iff $d_3=d_4=0$, i.e. $P$ is the vertex with the right angle, where $d_5=\frac{12}{5}$ is the altitude to the hypotenuse.

**Answer: $\frac{12}{5}$**

bmt-2016-individual-06.title: Period mod 5
bmt-2016-individual-06.body:
Modulo $5$ the sequence is $1,2,3,0,2,1,0,3$, and then it repeats (the next terms are $1,2,3$ again, and a three-term state determines everything). So the sequence has period $8$ with $2$ zeros per period. Indices $0,\dots,95$ contain $12$ periods: $24$ zeros; indices $96,\dots,100$ have residues $1,2,3,0,2$: one more zero. Total $25$.

**Answer: 25**

bmt-2016-individual-08.title: Difference of cubes
bmt-2016-individual-08.body:
Let $a=\sqrt[3]9$, $b=2$. Then $\sqrt[3]{81}=a^2$, $\sqrt[3]{72}=ab$, $\sqrt[3]{64}=4=b^2$. So the denominator is $a^2+ab+b^2=\frac{a^3-b^3}{a-b}=\frac{9-8}{a-b}$ and the expression is $a-b=\sqrt[3]9-2$.

**Answer: $\sqrt[3]{9}-2$**

bmt-2016-individual-09.title: Linearity of expectation
bmt-2016-individual-09.body:
A triangle with two sides parallel to the axes is a right triangle with axis-parallel legs. Choose the right-angle vertex ($25$ ways), another vertex in its row ($4$ ways) and one in its column ($4$ ways): $25\cdot16=400$ triangles. Each is monochromatic with probability $3\cdot\frac1{27}=\frac19$. Expected number: $\frac{400}{9}$.

**Answer: $\frac{400}{9}$**

bmt-2016-individual-11.title: Middle root
bmt-2016-individual-11.body:
Write the roots as $m-d,m,m+d$. Their sum is $3m=\frac32$, so $m=\frac12$. The product is $m(m^2-d^2)=-\frac38$, so $\frac14-d^2=-\frac34$ and $d=1$. The roots are $-\frac12,\frac12,\frac32$ (check: sum of pairwise products $-\frac14+(-\frac34)+\frac34=-\frac14$ ✓).

**Answer: $-\frac12,\frac12,\frac32$**

bmt-2016-individual-12.title: Stars and bars
bmt-2016-individual-12.body:
A nondecreasing sequence $1\le a_1\le\dots\le a_7\le9$ is a multiset of size $7$ from $9$ values: $\binom{9+7-1}{7}=\binom{15}{7}=6435$.

**Answer: 6435**

bmt-2016-individual-13.title: Difference polynomial
bmt-2016-individual-13.body:
The difference (quartic minus cubic) is a monic quartic $x^4+(2-a)x^3-20x^2+(8-b)x+(64-c)$ with roots $-6,-3,2$ and a fourth root $r$ (the fourth intersection). Its $x^2$ coefficient is $e_2=-20$: with roots $-6,-3,2,r$, $e_2=18-12-6+r(-6-3+2)=-7r$. So $-7r=-20$ and $r=\frac{20}{7}$.

**Answer: $\frac{20}{7}$**

bmt-2016-individual-14.title: Spread three points in a square
bmt-2016-individual-14.body:
The centers lie in a square of side $L=s-2$ and must be pairwise at least $2$ apart. Take centers $(0,0)$, $(L,t)$, $(t,L)$ (the optimal, symmetric arrangement of three points). Setting the distances equal to $2$: $\sqrt2(L-t)=2$ gives $t=L-\sqrt2$, and $L^2+t^2=4$ gives $L^2-\sqrt2L-1=0$, so $L=\frac{\sqrt2+\sqrt6}{2}$. (This is the known optimum: the largest possible minimum distance among $3$ points in a unit square is $\sqrt6-\sqrt2=\frac{2}{L}$.)

Hence $s=2+\frac{\sqrt2+\sqrt6}{2}\approx3.93$.

**Answer: $2+\frac{\sqrt2+\sqrt6}{2}$**

bmt-2016-individual-15.title: Each element lies in exactly two subsets
bmt-2016-individual-15.body:
Let $d_i$ be the number of chosen subsets containing element $i$. Then $\sum d_i=12$, and counting pairs of subsets (each pair shares exactly one element) gives $\sum\binom{d_i}{2}=\binom42=6$, i.e. $\sum d_i^2=24$. Then $\sum(d_i-2)^2=24-4\cdot12+24=0$, so every $d_i=2$.

Thus each element lies in exactly two of the four subsets, and each of the $6$ pairs of subsets shares exactly one element: this is a bijection between the $6$ elements and the $6$ pairs of subsets. Number the subsets $1,\dots,4$: there are $6!=720$ bijections, and since the subsets are unordered each collection is counted $4!=24$ times: $\frac{720}{24}=30$.

**Answer: 30**

bmt-2016-individual-16.title: Inradius
bmt-2016-individual-16.body:
$r=\frac{3V}{A}$. Here $V=\frac16$; the three coordinate faces have area $\frac12$ each and the slanted face (equilateral with side $\sqrt2$) has area $\frac{\sqrt3}{2}$, so $A=\frac{3+\sqrt3}{2}$. Then $r=\frac{1/2}{(3+\sqrt3)/2}=\frac1{3+\sqrt3}=\frac{3-\sqrt3}{6}$.

**Answer: $\frac{3-\sqrt3}{6}$**

bmt-2016-individual-17.title: Coordinates
bmt-2016-individual-17.body:
$AB=2$, $AC=\sqrt3$, so $B=(2,0)$ and $C=\left(\frac32,\frac{\sqrt3}2\right)$. The bisector from $C$ meets $AB$ at $E$ with $AE:EB=AC:CB=\sqrt3:1$, so $AE=\frac{2\sqrt3}{\sqrt3+1}=3-\sqrt3$ and $E=(3-\sqrt3,0)$. The slope of $CE$ is $\frac{\sqrt3/2}{\sqrt3-3/2}=2+\sqrt3$, so at $x=0$ the line has $y=-(2+\sqrt3)(3-\sqrt3)=-(3+\sqrt3)$: $D=(0,-3-\sqrt3)$.

Quadrilateral $ADBC$ is split by $AB$ into triangles $ADB$ and $ABC$: $[ADB]=\frac12\cdot2\cdot(3+\sqrt3)=3+\sqrt3$ and $[ABC]=\frac12\cdot\sqrt3\cdot1=\frac{\sqrt3}2$. Total $3+\frac{3\sqrt3}2$.

**Answer: $3+\frac{3\sqrt3}{2}$**

bmt-2016-individual-18.title: Counting lattice points
bmt-2016-individual-18.body:
$r_1+\dots+r_n$ counts the lattice points $(x,y)\ne(0,0)$ with $x^2+y^2\le n$, i.e. the lattice points in a disk of radius $\sqrt n$ except the origin. Their number is $\pi n+O(\sqrt n)$, so the limit is $\pi$.

**Answer: $\pi$**

bmt-2016-individual-19.title: Invariant
bmt-2016-individual-19.body:
$P_{n+1}=\frac14(P_n+P_{n-1}+P_{n-2}+P_{n-3})$. The vector $Q_n=4P_n+3P_{n-1}+2P_{n-2}+P_{n-3}$ is invariant: $Q_{n+1}=4P_{n+1}+3P_n+2P_{n-1}+P_{n-2}=Q_n$. Hence $P_\infty=\frac{Q_4}{10}=\frac{4P_4+3P_3+2P_2+P_1}{10}$.

Then $P_5-P_\infty=\frac{P_1+P_2+P_3+P_4}{4}-P_\infty=\frac{3P_1+P_2-P_3-3P_4}{20}$. For coefficients $c_i$ summing to $0$, $\left|\sum c_iP_i\right|^2=-\sum_{i<j}c_ic_j|P_iP_j|^2=-e_2(c)$ when all distances are $1$; for $c=(3,1,-1,-3)$, $e_2=3-3-9-1-3+3=-10$. So $|P_5P_\infty|=\frac{\sqrt{10}}{20}$.

**Answer: $\frac{\sqrt{10}}{20}$**

bmt-2016-individual-20.title: Roots of unity
bmt-2016-individual-20.body:
$e^{i\theta}\cdot2\cos\theta=e^{i\theta}(e^{i\theta}+e^{-i\theta})=1+e^{2i\theta}$. So the product is $\prod_{k=1}^{2017}(1+\omega^k)$ with $\omega=e^{2\pi i/2017}$. The $k=2017$ factor is $2$. For $k=1,\dots,2016$, $\prod(x-\omega^k)=1+x+\dots+x^{2016}$; at $x=-1$ this is $1$, so $\prod(-1-\omega^k)=1$ and, since there are $2016$ factors (an even number), $\prod(1+\omega^k)=1$. Total: $2$.

**Answer: 2**
